candidate.title: Exploiting Tree Structure for Credit Assignment in Reinforcement Learning with Large Language Models.
candidate.abstract: Reinforcement learning has shown strong promise for strengthening the reasoning ability of large language models (LLMs), but sparse, delayed rewards over long chains make token-level credit assignment a central challenge. Actor-critic methods like PPO provide token-level credit but require training a value network alongside the policy, which introduces complexity and can encourage overfitting. Critic-free alternatives such as GRPO avoid this burden but rely on sequence-level outcomes, distributing a single reward uniformly across tokens and ignoring structural differences between responses. We propose Prefix-to-Tree (P2T), which organizes the sampled responses of a prompt into a prefix tree and computes nonparametric prefix values by aggregating descendant outcomes. Building on this idea, we develop TEMPO (Tree-Estimated Mean Prefix Value for Policy Optimization), a critic-free algorithm that enriches GRPO with branch-aware temporal-difference (TD) corrections. Across Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-4B, TEMPO consistently improves both convergence and final performance over PPO and GRPO on in-distribution benchmarks (MATH, MedQA) and out-of-distribution settings (GSM-HARD, AMC23, MedMCQA, MMLU-Medical), achieving higher validation accuracy within comparable wall-clock time.
candidate.authors: Tran H, Yao Z, Yu H.

extraction.summary: 针对长链推理中稀疏延迟奖励导致token级信用分配困难、PPO需训练价值网络而GRPO仅用序列级结果的问题，提出Prefix-to-Tree（P2T）与TEMPO。P2T把同一提示的采样响应组织成前缀树，通过聚合后代结果计算非参数前缀值；TEMPO在此基础上为GRPO加入分支感知的时序差分修正，无需critic。在Qwen3-1.7B与Qwen3-4B上，TEMPO在MATH、MedQA等分布内及GSM-HARD、AMC23、MedMCQA、MMLU-Medical等分布外基准上，收敛与最终性能均持续优于PPO和GRPO，并在相当墙钟时间内取得更高验证准确率。
